title: Deciding within a space bound
statement: A finite Turing machine $M$ decides a language $L$ of Boolean strings within space bound $s$ if, on every Boolean input string $x$, it computes the one-symbol Boolean indicator of whether $x$ belongs to $L$, using at most $s(|x|)$ space.
hypotheses_covered: A finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
A space bound from natural input lengths to natural numbers
For every Boolean input string, the machine computes the membership indicator and satisfies the space bound
